newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money eases as demand abates.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money eases as demand abates.

text.p: The Philippine call rate eased to 10.8125 percent from Thursday's 11.0625 percent as demand for pesos slowed down, traders said.
"Many of the banks have squared their positions earlier in the week," a trader said, referring to the end-of-week liquidity reporting by commercial banks.
He added that the steady buying of dollars by the Central Bank in the past days had infused pesos into the system.
Another trader said most banks have already beefed up their deposit bases in time for the year-end financial book closing.
Turnover in the interbank market dwindled further to 17.056 billion pesos from yesterday's 19.451 billion pesos.
Done rates ranged from 10.78125 percent, just higher than the Central Bank's benchmark rate of 10.75 percent, to a high of 11.0 percent.
The secondary rates for government securities were mostly unchanged due to little demand from banks.
"Banks were not buying bills for their own inventories. Most of the buying was just to service their clients," another trader said.
Three-month bills were being bid between 11.5 to 11.65 percent and offered at 11.35 to 11.525 percent.

Six-month bills were being bid between 11.825 to 12.0 percent and offered at 11.65 to 11.825 percent, while the one-year bills were being bid at 12.25 to 12.5 percent and offered at 12.1 to 12.225 percent.
